descs.t: Flavio Bolsonaro and his family will receive US visas after he left Brazil, the State Department says. He lost Sunday's presidential election to Lula da Silva, and a Supreme Court order told him to hand over his passports, which were then cancelled. We walk through how he left, what Washington said and what Brazil's courts are investigating.

Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil for the United States after losing to Lula, and the State Department says he and his family will get visas. Brazil's Supreme Court had ordered his passports surrendered and opened an investigation into alleged foreign funding, while Trump said he would approve his coming. We look at what each side claims and what it means for the US and Brazil.

Flavio Bolsonaro, who reportedly won nearly 60 million votes, defied a passport order from Justice Alexandre de Moraes and left Brazil, and Washington is giving his family visas. His allies call it political persecution by the Lula government, while Brazil's courts point to investigations. We lay out the passport order, the investigations and why the US stepped in.

intro.plain: Big one out of Brazil. Flavio Bolsonaro lost Sunday's presidential election to Lula, a Supreme Court justice ordered him to hand over his passports, he did not, and now he is out of the country. The State Department says he and his family will get US visas. So, chat: should Washington be taking in Brazil's defeated candidate, yes or no?
intro.mid: Flavio Bolsonaro is out of Brazil. Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered his passports surrendered, they were cancelled when he did not, and the State Department now says he and his family get US visas. Trump says he approves and calls the election really strange. Brazil's court is investigating alleged foreign funding. Chat, is this justice in Brazil or a crackdown on the opposition?
intro.bold: Lula wins, and within days his main rival is out of the country. Flavio Bolsonaro's allies say an order to keep him in Brazil came seven minutes after Lula was declared the winner. He refused to hand over his passports, he left, and Washington is giving his family visas. Trump says he would approve. Chat, is Brazil now punishing people for running against Lula?

hook.plain: Flavio Bolsonaro lost to Lula, was told to surrender his passports, and left Brazil anyway. Now the State Department says his family gets US visas. Here is how it happened.
hook.mid: A court order, cancelled passports and a flight out: Flavio Bolsonaro is gone, and the US is giving him visas. Here is what each side says and what it means for Washington and Brazil.
hook.bold: Days after Lula won, his rival's passports were cancelled. Flavio Bolsonaro left anyway, and America is opening the door. This is how Brazil's opposition leader ended up in exile.

descs.t: Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc is slightly ahead in Israel's election with about 70% of votes counted, but it is still short of a majority. His main rival is opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot. We walk through where the count stands, what a majority needs and what happens if neither side reaches it.

Israel's election is down to the wire: Netanyahu's bloc leads Gadi Eisenkot with most votes counted, and one exit poll projects 61 seats, exactly the majority line. Reports still say the bloc is short as counting continues. We look at the numbers, the coalition math and what happens if neither side gets there.

Some called Netanyahu beaten, and now his bloc leads Israel's election. With about 70% counted it is just short of a majority, one exit poll projects 61 seats, and Eisenkot says no to another election. We break down the count, the coalition math and what comes next.

intro.plain: Israel's election is still being counted. With about 70% of the votes in, Netanyahu's bloc is slightly ahead of Gadi Eisenkot, but it is not yet at a majority. One exit poll now projects 61 seats for the bloc, which is exactly the line. So, chat: does Netanyahu get there, or does Israel end up stuck again?
intro.mid: Here is where Israel stands. Netanyahu's bloc leads Eisenkot with about 70% counted, one exit poll projects 61 seats, and other reports say it is still short of a majority. Eisenkot says no to another election. Every seat matters now. Chat, does Netanyahu reach 61, or does Israel vote again?
intro.bold: They said Netanyahu was finished. With about 70% of the vote counted, his bloc is ahead in Israel. It is still just short of a majority, one exit poll gives it 61 seats, and Eisenkot is already saying no to another election. This is going down to the last seat. Chat, is this the comeback, yes or no?

hook.bold: They called him finished. Now Netanyahu's bloc leads Israel's vote and sits just short of a majority. Here is how close it is and why every seat counts.

descs.t: James Talarico and Donald Trump held dueling rallies in Texas in the final days of the Senate race, with Trump backing Ken Paxton in Lubbock. Early voting is almost over and both sides say turnout will decide it. We walk through the race, the rallies and what each side is telling Texans.

Trump told a Texas crowd he needs Ken Paxton in the Senate, while Democrat James Talarico held his own rallies in the race's final days. Paxton calls Talarico the most radical Democrat ever to run statewide in Texas, and one Republican warns they are getting beat in the early vote. We look at the turnout claims and what the seat means for the Senate.

Trump went after James Talarico's platform in Texas, calling him obsessed with turning young boys and girls transgender, and said he needs Ken Paxton in the Senate. Paxton says this election decides whether Texas stays Texas. We break down Talarico's record, the early vote numbers and why Republicans are not taking this seat for granted.

intro.plain: Texas is in its final days and it is rally against rally. Trump was in Lubbock backing Ken Paxton for Senate, and Democrat James Talarico is out with rallies of his own. Early voting is almost over, and both sides say turnout decides it. So, chat: are you calling this one for Paxton or for Talarico?
intro.mid: Trump says it plainly: I need the help of Ken Paxton in the U.S. Senate. He is doing rallies in Texas for him, Paxton calls Talarico the most radical Democrat ever to run statewide there, and one Republican says they are getting beat in the early vote. Chat, is Texas really in play, or is this a scare to drive turnout?
intro.bold: Trump just went after James Talarico in front of a Texas crowd, and he did not hold back. He says he needs Ken Paxton in the Senate, Paxton says Texas stays Texas or it does not, and Republicans are warning about the early vote. This seat matters for the whole Senate. Chat, would Texas really send Talarico to Washington?

hook.plain: Trump and James Talarico held dueling rallies in Texas with early voting almost over. Here is where the Senate race stands and what each side is saying.
hook.mid: Trump says he needs Ken Paxton in the Senate, and one Republican says they are getting beat in the early vote. Here is how close Texas really is.
hook.bold: Trump tore into James Talarico's platform in Texas and asked voters to send Ken Paxton to the Senate. Here is why Republicans are fighting this hard for a red state.

Trump says Putin and Zelenskyy will be in a meeting soon, while his administration reportedly weighs lifting sanctions on Russia's sovereign wealth fund. Is this the road to peace, or does Putin get relief before he gives anything? We break down the summit plan and the sanctions question.

descs.t: Trump went after Abdul El-Sayed, the Democrat running for Senate in Michigan against Mike Rogers, saying Sharia law is never coming to America. The race has turned on an antisemitic ad and on who is paying for what. We walk through the claims, the money and where the race stands.

The Michigan Senate race between Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers has become a fight over antisemitism and money. Critics say El-Sayed never truly disavowed an antisemitic ad, Republicans say he took donations from a Muslim Brotherhood spokesman, and Bernie Sanders points to AIPAC spending $9 million for Rogers. We look at each claim and what it means for the seat.

Trump told Abdul El-Sayed that Sharia law is never coming to America, and the charges against his campaign keep coming: an antisemitic ad critics say he never disavowed, anti-Israel ads Mike Rogers says Hasan Piker's uncle is funding, and a donation Republicans tie to the Muslim Brotherhood. We break down what is on record and why this seat matters.

descs.t: Israel detained a group of MPs and an MSP and barred them from entering the West Bank, the BBC reports. We walk through what is known about the detention, the entry ban and what it means for the lawmakers involved.

Israel detained MPs and an MSP and barred them from entering the West Bank, the BBC reports, and critics online are using it to repeat the apartheid charge. We look at the entry ban, the arguments on both sides of it and what Israel's control of entry means in practice.

Israel detained MPs and an MSP and refused them entry to the West Bank, and the apartheid accusations followed within hours. Who gets in is Israel's decision, and we lay out the case for it, what is actually known about this detention and why the outrage online goes far beyond the facts.

intro.plain: Israel has detained a group of MPs and an MSP and barred them from entering the West Bank, according to the BBC. We do not have much detail yet on why. I want to walk through what we know. So, chat: should a country be able to refuse entry to foreign lawmakers, yes or no?
